summary: Cross-language idempotency key mismatch causing duplicate remote tool invocations during function-calling retries
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate external tool invocations when using function-calling across multiple SDKs. The customer issues a request from their TypeScript frontend that is proxied by a backend implemented in Python. Both sides attach an idempotency key, but when the backend retries on an internal 5xx, the function executor receives two invocations for the same logical request.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends chat completion with function-calling from TS client to backend API (TS -> Python proxy -> Redwood API)
2) TS client includes X-Idempotency-Key header and body.metadata.idempotency_key set to same value
3) Python backend attaches its own idempotency header based on incoming header and forwards request to Redwood using python-sdk call.function_call()
4) Simulate transient 502 from serving-runtime (we injected a kill to a replica) so backend performs exponential backoff retry
5) Observe two invocations executed by function-executor service within 2s window despite keys matching
Expected: single function invocation (at-most-once) observed for the idempotency key. Actual: duplicate invocations observed and customer sees duplicate side effects (two emails sent).
raw_logs:
[2026-03-10T14:02:07Z] api-gateway: received request id=abc123 header X-Idempotency-Key=snz-001
[2026-03-10T14:02:07Z] python-proxy: forwarded request to /v1/chat.func idempotency=snz-001 trace=trace-77
[2026-03-10T14:02:07Z] serving-runtime: returned 502 'upstream timeout' for req trace-77
[2026-03-10T14:02:08Z] python-proxy: retry attempt 1 for idempotency=snz-001
[2026-03-10T14:02:08Z] serving-runtime: accepted request trace-78 -> dispatched to function-executor invocation-id=fex-443
[2026-03-10T14:02:09Z] function-executor: executed tool send_email invocation-id=fex-443 status=success
[2026-03-10T14:02:09Z] function-executor: executed tool send_email invocation-id=fex-444 status=success (duplicate)
Notes: invocation-id differs even though idempotency header present.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: idempotency keys from TS and Python layers were not normalized and were being interpreted as different keys by the API. Reproduction verified duplicates when backend retries after a transient 502. Traced headers across gateway and serving-runtime: both requests carried X-Idempotency-Key but python-sdk was also attaching a SDK-generated internal idempotency token in request body.metadata which the server prioritizes. The server dedup key resolution order currently prefers body.metadata.idempotency_key when present and falls back to X-Idempotency-Key; in this flow the first attempt had body.metadata absent and second (retry) had body.metadata populated by the python-sdk client wrapper. This caused server to treat them as distinct.
Additional findings: TypeScript client included idempotency in both header and body; Python client SDK auto-populates body.metadata when header is present unless explicit flag disabled. Race condition: transient error path where the forwarded first request did not include body.metadata (proxy stripped it), but retry path had SDK repopulate body.metadata resulting in two different dedup keys.
Impact: customer experienced duplicate side effects (two transactional emails). Occurred for ~0.2% of function-calling flows in their traffic pattern under transient upstream errors. Reproducible in staging with proxy that conditionally strips metadata.
comments: Support - Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Customer reported duplicate emails tied to a single user action. They pasted logs showing two function-executor invocations. Customer is on dedicated plan and requests urgency due to user impact.

SRE - Marco Nguyen (2026-03-10): Reproduced in staging. Confirmed two invocations and differing internal dedup keys. Noted the serving-runtime dedup priority ordering in code. Created a short reproduction script using ts-client -> python-proxy -> python-sdk.

SDK Eng - Priya Shah (2026-03-11): Observed python-sdk behavior: auto-populates body.metadata.idempotency_key if X-Idempotency-Key header present unless options.disable_metadata_injection=true. This was inconsistent with TS SDK which always attaches both. Opened PR to make metadata injection behaviour explicit and documented.

Backend Eng - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-11): Added a temporary server-side normalization in gateway: normalize dedup key by checking both header and body and preferring the earliest-seen non-empty value. Deployed to staging; duplicate no longer reproducible in controlled tests.
Customer - SparkNotez (2026-03-11): Confirmed that disabling backend retry eliminates duplicates, but they need retries for resiliency. Asked for recommended pattern for multi-hop architectures.
Support - Aisha Patel (2026-03-12): Advised customer on interim workaround (proxy must preserve header-to-body mapping or set python-sdk disable flag). Working on coordinated SDK + server fix.

Engineering - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12): ETA for full fix: server-side dedup normalization + SDK patch to make metadata injection consistent across languages. Targeted rollout: canary 2026-03-18, full 2026-03-22.
resolution: Workaround provided to customer: (1) ensure proxy preserves original X-Idempotency-Key header and does not inject or remove body.metadata on the first attempt, or (2) set python-sdk option disable_metadata_injection=true to avoid body metadata being added only on retry. Temporary gateway normalization deployed to staging to reduce immediate duplicates. Engineering plan: add server normalization that canonicalizes dedup keys (prefer header if both present but accept either) and ship python-sdk patch to align behavior with TS SDK. Rollout schedule created; post-deploy monitoring dashboard added. Customer accepted workaround and will validate on staging before full rollout.
next_steps: 1) Merge and release python-sdk patch that documents and exposes metadata injection toggle (PR #1876). 2) Implement canonicalization in gateway to resolve mixed-key scenarios and add unit/integration tests. 3) Add a synthetic test in CI that simulates proxy stripping body.metadata to catch regressions. 4) Customer validation call scheduled 2026-03-13. 5) Monitor for duplicates for two weeks after full rollout.
notes_for_postmortem: If duplicates continue after fixes, track per-request trace across gateway + serving + executor to determine whether dedup keys were normalized; include exact header/body snapshots. Consider an API change that requires a single canonical idempotency header with SDK adapters performing mapping consistently.
